title: nf-core/sarek pipeline parameters
description: An open-source analysis pipeline to detect germline or somatic variants from whole genome or targeted sequencing

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.
input_output_options.help_text: Specify input samplesheet, step and output folder.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about the samples in the experiment.
input.help_text:
A design file with information about the samples in your experiment. Use this parameter to specify the location of the input files. It has to be a comma-separated file with a header row. See [usage docs](https://nf-co.re/sarek/usage#input).

If no input file is specified, sarek will attempt to locate one in the `{outdir}` directory. If no input should be supplied, i.e. when --step is supplied or --build_only_index, then set --input false

step.help_text: The pipeline starts from this step and then runs through the possible subsequent steps.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

main_options.title: Main options
main_options.description: Most common options used for the pipeline

split_fastq.description: Specify how many reads each split of a FastQ file contains. Set 0 to turn off splitting at all.
split_fastq.help_text:
Uses fastp to split FASTQ files by number of reads, parallelising alignment across the shards. Note that a non-zero value runs fastp even with every trimming step off, and fastp's read-level quality filter then still applies (as in upstream sarek) unless `--filter_quality false`; adapter trimming stays off and poly-G trimming follows fastp's read-name auto-detection (NextSeq/NovaSeq names), as in upstream. Although the minimum value is 250 reads, if you have fewer than 250 reads a single FASTQ shard will still be created. Every ALE profile sets 0.

fastp: `--split_by_lines` / `-S` with 4 x this value.

nucleotides_per_second.help_text:
Intervals are parts of the chopped up genome used to speed up preprocessing and variant calling. See `--intervals` for more info. 

Changing this parameter, changes the number of intervals that are grouped and processed together. Bed files from target sequencing can contain thousands or small intervals. Spinning up a new process for each can be quite resource intensive. Instead it can be desired to process small intervals together on larger nodes. 
In order to make use of this parameter, no runtime estimate can be present in the bed file (column 5).

intervals.help_text:
To speed up preprocessing and variant calling processes, the execution is parallelized across a reference chopped into smaller pieces.

Parts of preprocessing and variant calling are done by these intervals, the different resulting files are then merged.
This can parallelize processes, and push down wall clock time significantly.

We are aligning to the whole genome, and then run Base Quality Score Recalibration and Variant Calling on the supplied regions.

**Whole Genome Sequencing:**

The (provided) intervals are chromosomes cut at their centromeres (so each chromosome arm processed separately) also additional unassigned contigs.

We are ignoring the `hs37d5` contig that contains concatenated decoy sequences.

The calling intervals can be defined using a .list or a BED file.
A .list file contains one interval per line in the format `chromosome:start-end` (1-based coordinates).
A BED file must be a tab-separated text file with one interval per line.
There must be at least three columns: chromosome, start, and end (0-based coordinates).
Additionally, the score column of the BED file can be used to provide an estimate of how many seconds it will take to call variants on that interval.
The fourth column remains unused.

```
|chr1|10000|207666|NA|47.3|
```
This indicates that variant calling on the interval chr1:10001-207666 takes approximately 47.3 seconds.

The runtime estimate is used in two different ways.
First, when there are multiple consecutive intervals in the file that take little time to compute, they are processed as a single job, thus reducing the number of processes that needs to be spawned.
Second, the jobs with largest processing time are started first, which reduces wall-clock time.
If no runtime is given, a time of 200000 nucleotides per second is assumed. See `--nucleotides_per_second` on how to customize this.
Actual figures vary from 2 nucleotides/second to 30000 nucleotides/second.
If you prefer, you can specify the full path to your reference genome when you run the pipeline:

> **NB** If none provided, will be generated automatically from the FASTA reference
> **NB** Use --no_intervals to disable automatic generation.

**Targeted Sequencing:**

The recommended flow for targeted sequencing data is to use the workflow as it is, but also provide a `BED` file containing targets for all steps using the `--intervals` option. In addition, the parameter `--wes` should be set.
It is advised to pad the variant calling regions (exons or target) to some extent before submitting to the workflow.

The procedure is similar to whole genome sequencing, except that only BED file are accepted. See above for formatting description.
Adding every exon as an interval in case of `WES` can generate >200K processes or jobs, much more forks, and similar number of directories in the Nextflow work directory. These are appropriately  grouped together to reduce number of processes run in parallel (see above and `--nucleotides_per_second` for details). 
Furthermore, primers and/or baits are not 100% specific, (certainly not for MHC and KIR, etc.), quite likely there going to be reads mapping to multiple locations.
If you are certain that the target is unique for your genome (all the reads will certainly map to only one location), and aligning to the whole genome is an overkill, it is actually better to change the reference itself.
intervals.description: Path to target bed file in case of whole exome or targeted sequencing or intervals file.

no_intervals.help_text:
Intervals are parts of the chopped up genome used to speed up preprocessing and variant calling. See `--intervals` for more info. 

If  `--no_intervals` is set no intervals will be taken into account for speed up or data processing.

wes.description: Enable when exome or panel data is provided.
wes.help_text: With this parameter flags in various tools are set for targeted sequencing data. It is recommended to enable for whole-exome and panel data analysis.

tools.description: Comma-separated list of tools to run. Tier-1 ALE recipe: `snpeff,cnvkit,tiddit,manta,haplotypecaller`.
tools.help_text:
Multiple tools separated with commas. All calling is **germline** — every sample carries `status = 0` in the samplesheet (see `docs/usage/input_samplesheet.md`); sarek's tumor-only and paired somatic modes are unused.

**Tier-1 (release-validated for ALE):**

- SNVs/Indels: `haplotypecaller` — GATK HaplotypeCaller, joint cohort calling per `experiment` (`--joint_germline`)
- Copy-number: `cnvkit`
- Structural variants: `manta`, `tiddit` — cohort-merged via SVDB
- Annotation: `snpeff` (custom cache)

Other sarek callers (`mutect2`, `freebayes`, `controlfreec`, ...) remain runnable but are Tier-2: functional, not release-validated for ALE.

skip_tools.help_text:
Multiple tools can be specified, separated by commas.

> **NB** `--skip_tools baserecalibrator_report` is actually just not saving the reports.
> **NB** `--skip_tools markduplicates_report` does not skip `MarkDuplicates` but prevent the collection of duplicate metrics that slows down performance.

fastq_preprocessing.title: Read preprocessing
fastq_preprocessing.description: Optional steps between the samplesheet and alignment, in run order: step 0 UMI consensus (fgbio, only with umi_read_structure) → fastp: step 1 adapter trimming · step 2 quality trimming per read end · step 3 read filtering. Reads are aligned exactly as sequenced unless a step is switched on; fastp runs only when step 1 or 2 is on (or split_fastq > 0). Details: docs/usage/read_preprocessing.md

umi_read_structure.description: Step 0 · UMI consensus: UMI read structure (enables the fgbio consensus step before fastp). Not used for ALE libraries.
umi_read_structure.help_text:
One structure if UMI is present on one end (i.e. '+T 2M11S+T'), or two structures separated by a blank space if UMIs a present on both ends (i.e. '2M11S+T 2M11S+T'); please note, this does not handle duplex-UMIs.

For more info on UMI usage in the pipeline, also check docs [here](./docs/usage/#how-to-handle-umis).

group_by_umi_strategy.description: Step 0 · UMI consensus: fgbio grouping strategy (Identity, Edit, Adjacency, Paired).
group_by_umi_strategy.help_text: Available values: Identity, Edit, Adjacency, Paired

trim_adapter.description: Step 1 · Adapter trimming: run fastp to remove adapter read-through (and, by default, apply step 3's read filter).
trim_adapter.help_text:
Adapters are found without any input: paired reads are trimmed wherever the two mates overlap, and `--detect_adapter_for_pe` infers the adapter sequence from the data for pairs that do not overlap. Set `adapter_sequence` to name the kit's adapter explicitly (useful when fastp reports `unspecified`).

Behaves as upstream sarek's `trim_fastq` (kept as a deprecated alias): fastp also applies its read-level quality filter unless `--filter_quality false` (step 3). Poly-G trimming follows fastp's own read-name rule unless `trim_nextseq` forces it (see that parameter). See docs/usage/read_preprocessing.md.

fastp: adapter trimming is fastp's default; off = `--disable_adapter_trimming` / `-A`. The module always adds `--detect_adapter_for_pe`.

trim_fastq.description: Deprecated alias of `trim_adapter` (upstream sarek name) - same behaviour, warns at startup.
trim_fastq.help_text: Kept so upstream-shaped params files keep working. Use `--trim_adapter`.

adapter_sequence.description: Step 1 · Adapter trimming: adapter sequence for read 1 (fastp `--adapter_sequence`). Leave empty to auto-detect.
adapter_sequence.help_text:
Only used with `--trim_adapter`. By default fastp finds adapters itself: paired reads are trimmed wherever the two mates overlap (`--detect_adapter_for_pe`), plus a sequence it infers from the data. On libraries with little adapter read-through that inference can fail (fastp then reports `unspecified`), and read pairs that do not overlap keep their adapter; giving the sequence explicitly closes that gap. Common values: Nextera/Tn5 `CTGTCTCTTATACACATCT`, TruSeq read 1 `AGATCGGAAGAGCACACGTCTGAACTCCAGTCA`.

fastp: `--adapter_sequence` / `-a`.

adapter_sequence_r2.description: Step 1 · Adapter trimming: adapter sequence for read 2 (fastp `--adapter_sequence_r2`). Defaults to `adapter_sequence`.
adapter_sequence_r2.help_text:
Only used with `--trim_adapter`. Nextera libraries use the same sequence on both reads, so this is normally left empty; TruSeq read 2 is `AGATCGGAAGAGCGTCGTGTAGGGAAAGAGTGT`.

fastp: `--adapter_sequence_r2`.

trim_nextseq.description: Step 1 · Adapter trimming: force poly-G tail trimming (fastp `--trim_poly_g`); any non-zero value enables it. At 0 fastp decides from the read names, as in upstream sarek.
trim_nextseq.help_text:
Poly-G tails come from two-colour chemistry (NextSeq/NovaSeq), where no signal reads as G. At 0 nothing is passed and fastp applies its own rule: poly-G trimming switches on automatically when the first read name carries a NextSeq/NovaSeq instrument prefix (e.g. `@A00123:...`) and stays off otherwise - so data renamed by SRA (`@SRR...`) is never poly-G-trimmed unless you set this. Any non-zero value forces it on for every dataset. The value itself is not passed to fastp (this is not Trim Galore's `--nextseq=X` quality cutoff); use `trim_quality_3prime` for quality trimming.

fastp: non-zero = `--trim_poly_g` / `-g`; 0 = nothing passed (fastp's read-name auto-detection; `--disable_trim_poly_g` / `-G` is not exposed).

trim_quality_3prime.description: Step 2 · Quality trimming, 3' end: trim a variable number of low-quality bases from the 3' end - `tail` (stop at the first good window) or `right` (cut at the first bad window and everything after it). Off when unset.
trim_quality_3prime.help_text:
fastp inspects `trim_quality_window` bases at a time and trims where their mean quality is below `trim_quality_mean` - no fixed number of bases.

```
read    5' ----------------------------> 3'
quality    high ... dip ... high .. low tail
tail    keep ####################### trim ..
right   keep ######## trim ................
```



- `tail`: Trimmomatic `TRAILING` with a window. The usual choice for 3'-end quality decay; a mid-read dip is left alone.
- `right`: Trimmomatic `SLIDINGWINDOW`. Stricter: a mid-read quality dip removes the rest of the read.

On the ottilie test set `tail` at 4/Q20 removed 0.03% (evolved clone) to 2.2% (parent) of bases beyond the adapters; `right` 3-4x more, because the parent has a systematic quality dip at position 58. Schematic and measurements: docs/usage/read_preprocessing.md.

Runs fastp on its own if `--trim_adapter` is off. Reads shorter than `length_required` after trimming are discarded (step 3). `right` supersedes `tail` in fastp, hence one choice.

fastp: `tail` = `--cut_tail` / `-3`; `right` = `--cut_right` / `-r`. Per-end overrides `--cut_tail_window_size`, `--cut_tail_mean_quality`, `--cut_right_*` are not exposed (shared `-W`/`-M` apply).

trim_quality_5prime.description: Step 2 · Quality trimming, 5' end: trim a variable number of low-quality bases from the 5' end (fastp `--cut_front`, Trimmomatic `LEADING`). Off by default.
trim_quality_5prime.help_text:
Same window/threshold as the 3' end (`trim_quality_window`, `trim_quality_mean`): walk in from the 5' end and stop at the first window whose mean quality passes. Rarely needed on Illumina data, where quality is lowest at the 3' end. Can be combined with `trim_quality_3prime`. See docs/usage/read_preprocessing.md.

fastp: `--cut_front` / `-5`.

trim_quality_mean.description: Step 2 · Quality trimming: mean Phred quality a window must reach to survive (fastp `--cut_mean_quality`), both ends.
trim_quality_mean.help_text:
Ignored unless a `trim_quality_*` end is set. 20 with a window of 4 is the Trimmomatic `SLIDINGWINDOW:4:20` / `TRAILING:20` convention.

fastp: `--cut_mean_quality` / `-M` (range 1-36).

trim_quality_window.description: Step 2 · Quality trimming: window size in bases (fastp `--cut_window_size`), both ends.
trim_quality_window.help_text:
Ignored unless a `trim_quality_*` end is set. 1 makes the trimming per-base (exactly Trimmomatic `TRAILING`/`LEADING`).

fastp: `--cut_window_size` / `-W` (range 1-1000).

clip_r1.description: Step 2 (fixed-count alternative): remove this many bp from the 5' end of read 1 (fastp `--trim_front1`).

clip_r2.description: Step 2 (fixed-count alternative): remove this many bp from the 5' end of read 2 (fastp `--trim_front2`).

three_prime_clip_r1.description: Step 2 (fixed-count alternative): remove this many bp from the 3' end of read 1 (fastp `--trim_tail1`); applied before the quality cut.

three_prime_clip_r2.description: Step 2 (fixed-count alternative): remove this many bp from the 3' end of read 2 (fastp `--trim_tail2`); applied before the quality cut.

filter_quality.description: Step 3 · Read filtering: discard read pairs with too many low-quality bases (fastp's read-level filter; thresholds below). On by default whenever fastp runs, as in upstream sarek.
filter_quality.help_text:
fastp's own default filter, evaluated on the trimmed read: a read is discarded, together with its mate, when more than `filter_quality_percent` of its bases are below `filter_quality_phred` (or it has more than 5 N). Applies whenever fastp runs - step 1, step 2 or `split_fastq > 0` - exactly as in upstream sarek 3.5.1, which has no switch for it. `--filter_quality false` passes `--disable_quality_filtering`, so trimming or splitting never removes whole reads (only `length_required` still does). On the ottilie test set the filter removes 0.7% (evolved clone) to 4.2% (parent) of read pairs; the counts are in `reports/fastp/<sample>/*.fastp.json` under `filtering_result`. See docs/usage/read_preprocessing.md.

fastp: on = `--qualified_quality_phred` / `-q` + `--unqualified_percent_limit` / `-u` (values from the two parameters below; N limit stays at fastp's `-n 5`); off = `--disable_quality_filtering` / `-Q`.

filter_quality_phred.description: Step 3 · Read filtering: a base counts as qualified at or above this Phred quality (fastp `--qualified_quality_phred`).
filter_quality_phred.help_text:
fastp's default is 15. Only used when `filter_quality` is on.

fastp: `--qualified_quality_phred` / `-q`.

filter_quality_percent.description: Step 3 · Read filtering: discard a read pair when more than this percentage of a read's bases are unqualified (fastp `--unqualified_percent_limit`).
filter_quality_percent.help_text:
fastp's default is 40. Only used when `filter_quality` is on.

fastp: `--unqualified_percent_limit` / `-u` (0-100).

length_required.description: Step 3 · Read filtering: discard reads shorter than this after trimming (fastp `--length_required`).
length_required.help_text:
fastp's default is 15 bp. A pair is discarded when either mate is too short. Always applied when fastp runs, independent of `filter_quality`.

fastp: `--length_required` / `-l`; the length filter itself can only be disabled by fastp's `-L`, which is not exposed.

save_trimmed.description: Outputs: publish the trimmed FASTQ files (preprocessing/fastp/<sample>/).

save_split_fastqs.description: Outputs: publish the split FASTQ shards (split_fastq > 0). Intended for testing.

reference_genome_options.title: Reference genome options

genome.help_text:
If using a reference genome configured in the pipeline using iGenomes, use this parameter to give the ID for the reference. This is then used to build the full paths for all required reference genome files e.g. `--genome GRCh38`.

See the [nf-core website docs](https://nf-co.re/usage/reference_genomes) for more details.

germline_resource.help_text:
The germline resource VCF file (bgzipped and tabixed) needed by GATK4 Mutect2 is a collection of calls that are likely present in the sample, with allele frequencies.
The AF info field must be present.
You can find a smaller, stripped gnomAD VCF file (most of the annotation is removed and only calls signed by PASS are stored) in the AWS iGenomes Annotation/GermlineResource folder.

If you use AWS iGenomes, this has already been set for you appropriately.

sentieon_dnascope_model.description: Machine learning model for Sentieon Dnascope.
sentieon_dnascope_model.help_text:
It is recommended to use DNAscope with a machine learning model to perform variant calling with higher accuracy by improving the candidate detection and filtering. Sentieon can provide you with a model trained using a subset of the data from the GiAB truth-set found in https://github.com/genome-in-a-bottle. In addition, Sentieon can assist you in the creation of models using your own data, which will calibrate the specifics of your sequencing and bio-informatics processing.

If you use AWS iGenomes, this has already been set for you appropriately.

genbank.description: Reference file for breseq (GenBank, GFF3, or FASTA format).
genbank.help_text: Path to a reference file used by breseq for variant calling. breseq accepts GenBank (.gb/.gbk), GFF3 (.gff3), or FASTA (.fasta) format. GenBank or GFF3 is recommended for annotation support.

report_gff3.description: Gene-annotation GFF3 for the mutation-report gene track (used when --generate_reports).
report_gff3.help_text: Per-genome GFF3 providing the gene track shown in the igv-reports dashboards. Optional — if omitted, reports are still generated without the gene annotation track.

breseq_args.help_text: Extra command-line arguments to pass to breseq. For example, use '--polymorphism-frequency-cutoff 0.1' to adjust the population mode frequency cutoff.

reference_genome_options.help_text:
The pipeline config files come bundled with paths to the Illumina iGenomes reference index files.
The configuration is set up to use the AWS-iGenomes resource
cf https://ewels.github.io/AWS-iGenomes/.

aligner.description: Specify aligner to be used to map reads to reference genome.
aligner.help_text:
Sarek will build missing indices automatically if not provided. Set `--bwa false` if indices should be (re-)built.
If DragMap is selected as aligner, it is recommended to skip baserecalibration with `--skip_tools baserecalibrator`. For more info see [here](https://gatk.broadinstitute.org/hc/en-us/articles/4407897446939--How-to-Run-germline-single-sample-short-variant-discovery-in-DRAGEN-mode).

save_mapped.help_text: If the parameter `--split-fastq` is used, the sharded bam files are merged and converted to CRAM before saving them.

save_output_as_bam.description: Saves output from mapping (if `--save_mapped`), Markduplicates & Baserecalibration as BAM file instead of CRAM

use_gatk_spark.description: Enable usage of GATK Spark implementation for duplicate marking and/or base quality score recalibration
use_gatk_spark.help_text:
Multiple separated with commas.

> The GATK4 Base Quality Score recalibration tools `Baserecalibrator` and `ApplyBQSR` are currently available as Beta release. Use with caution!

only_paired_variant_calling.description: If true, skips germline variant calling for matched normal to tumor sample. Normal samples without matched tumor will still be processed through germline variant calling tools.
only_paired_variant_calling.help_text: This can speed up computation for somatic variant calling with matched normal samples. If false, all normal samples are processed as well through the germline variantcalling tools. If true, only somatic variant calling is done.

ascat_min_base_qual.description: Overwrite Ascat min base quality required for a read to be counted.

ascat_min_counts.description: Overwrite Ascat minimum depth required in the normal for a SNP to be considered.

ascat_min_map_qual.description: Overwrite Ascat min mapping quality required for a read to be counted.

ascat_ploidy.help_text: ASCAT: optional argument to override ASCAT optimization and supply psi parameter (expert parameter, do not adapt unless you know what you are doing). See [here](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VanLoo-lab/ascat/master/man/ASCAT-manual.pdf)

ascat_purity.help_text:
Overwrites ASCAT's `rho_manual` parameter. Expert use only, see [here](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VanLoo-lab/ascat/master/man/ASCAT-manual.pdf) for details.
Requires that `--ascat_ploidy` is set.

cf_chrom_len.description: Specify a custom chromosome length file.
cf_chrom_len.help_text:
Control-FREEC requires a file containing all chromosome lenghts. By default the fasta.fai is used. If the fasta.fai file contains chromosomes not present in the intervals, it fails (see: https://github.com/BoevaLab/FREEC/issues/106).

In this case, a custom chromosome length can be specified. It must be of the same format as the fai, but only contain the relevant chromosomes.

cf_contamination.description: Design known contamination value for Control-FREEC

cf_minqual.description: Minimal sequencing quality for a position to be considered in BAF analysis.

cf_mincov.description: Minimal read coverage for a position to be considered in BAF analysis.

cf_ploidy.help_text: In case of doubt, you can set different values and Control-FREEC will select the one that explains most observed CNAs Example: ploidy=2 , ploidy=2,3,4. For more details, see the [manual](http://boevalab.inf.ethz.ch/FREEC/tutorial.html).

joint_germline.description: Turn on the joint germline variant calling for GATK haplotypecaller
joint_germline.help_text: Uses all normal germline samples (as designated by `status` in the input csv) in the joint germline variant calling process.

joint_manta.description: One multi-sample Manta germline run per experiment, every sample of the experiment genotyped at each candidate SV.
joint_manta.help_text:
Evidence-backed presence/absence in the cohort SV matrix: an event with weak evidence in one sample is reported as a genotype (with PR/SR read support and a per-sample FT) instead of being absent from that sample's VCF. Outputs publish under `variant_calling/manta/<experiment>/` and are split back to per-sample VCFs.

Joint SV calling is a single task per experiment whose cost grows with each added sample; intended for small cohorts (validated at 4 samples). For large samplesheets leave this off — per-sample Manta feeds the same cohort SV merge, only without explicit `0/0` genotypes at other samples' candidates.

Note: samplesheets with multiple experiments are untested in joint mode; planned development will move joint calling to all samples (matching joint HaplotypeCaller's cohort-wide behavior).

manta_high_sensitivity.description: Run Manta with its human-WGS repeat heuristics off: depth filters disabled (`--exome`) and graphNodeMaxEdgeCount = 0.
manta_high_sensitivity.help_text: Manta skips SV discovery in regions deeper than 3x the chromosome median and prunes junctions between breakend hubs linked to more than 10 other regions. Both assume a human genome and remove real junctions in engineered multi-copy constructs, amplified regions and Ty/LTR insertions. With this switch Manta reports them (no `MaxDepth` FILTER tag is written any more; depth is still in `INFO/BND_DEPTH`). Applies to every Manta run (per-sample or joint). Not a data-type flag: `--wes` stays false for WGS.

split_haplotypecaller_joint_vcf.description: Split HaplotypeCaller joint germline VCF into individual sample VCFs with renamed samples (removes patient prefix)
split_haplotypecaller_joint_vcf.help_text: When enabled with `--joint_germline`, extracts individual sample VCFs from the HaplotypeCaller joint calling output. Sample names in the output VCFs are renamed to remove the patient/experiment prefix (e.g., ALE_Exp1_Sample1 becomes Sample1). Useful for sample-specific annotation, comparison, or downstream analysis.

hard_filter_haplotypecaller_joint.description: Apply hard filtering to individual VCFs from HaplotypeCaller joint calling (requires --split_haplotypecaller_joint_vcf)
hard_filter_haplotypecaller_joint.help_text: When enabled, applies sample-specific quality filters (FORMAT/GQ>=20, FORMAT/DP>=8, FILTER=PASS) to individual VCFs extracted from joint calling. Removes failing variants entirely (no missing genotypes) for clean MultiQC reporting and variant count tracking. Output suffix: `.haplotypecaller.from_joint_calling_hard_filtered.vcf.gz`. Designed for ALE experiments to ensure per-sample quality.

generate_reports.description: Generate the ALE mutation-report dashboard (igv-reports) after variant calling.
generate_reports.help_text: Builds per-sample and cohort igv-reports dashboards from the HaplotypeCaller, Manta, TIDDIT and CNVKit outputs. Sections degrade gracefully if a tool was not run. The reference index is auto-generated if `--fasta_fai` is not supplied.

joint_mutect2.description: Runs Mutect2 in joint (multi-sample) mode for better concordance among variant calls of tumor samples from the same patient. Mutect2 outputs will be stored in a subfolder named with patient ID under `variant_calling/mutect2/` folder. Only a single normal sample per patient is allowed. Tumor-only mode is also supported.

ignore_soft_clipped_bases.description: Do not analyze soft clipped bases in the reads for GATK Mutect2.
ignore_soft_clipped_bases.help_text: use the `--dont-use-soft-clipped-bases` params with GATK Mutect2.

pon.help_text:
Without PON, there will be no calls with PASS in the INFO field, only an unfiltered VCF is written.
It is highly recommended to make your own PON, as it depends on sequencer and library preparation.

The pipeline is shipped with a panel-of-normals for `--genome GATK.GRCh38` provided by [GATK](https://gatk.broadinstitute.org/hc/en-us/articles/360035890631-Panel-of-Normals-PON-). 

See [PON documentation](https://gatk.broadinstitute.org/hc/en-us/articles/360042479112-CreateSomaticPanelOfNormals-BETA)
> **NB** PON file should be bgzipped.

pon_tbi.help_text: If none provided, will be generated automatically from the PON bgzipped VCF file.

sentieon_haplotyper_emit_mode.description: Option for selecting output and emit-mode of Sentieon's Haplotyper.
sentieon_haplotyper_emit_mode.help_text: The option `--sentieon_haplotyper_emit_mode` can be set to the same string values as the Haplotyper's `--emit_mode`. To output both a vcf and a gvcf, specify both a vcf-option (currently, `all`, `confident` and `variant`) and `gvcf`. For example, to obtain a vcf and gvcf one could set `--sentieon_haplotyper_emit_mode` to `variant, gvcf`.

sentieon_dnascope_emit_mode.description: Option for selecting output and emit-mode of Sentieon's Dnascope.
sentieon_dnascope_emit_mode.help_text: The option `--sentieon_dnascope_emit_mode` can be set to the same string values as the Dnascope's `--emit_mode`. To output both a vcf and a gvcf, specify both a vcf-option (currently, `all`, `confident` and `variant`) and `gvcf`. For example, to obtain a vcf and gvcf one could set `--sentieon_dnascope_emit_mode` to `variant, gvcf`.

sentieon_dnascope_pcr_indel_model.description: Option for selecting the PCR indel model used by Sentieon Dnascope.
sentieon_dnascope_pcr_indel_model.help_text: PCR indel model used to weed out false positive indels more or less aggressively. The possible MODELs are: NONE (used for PCR free samples), and HOSTILE, AGGRESSIVE and CONSERVATIVE, in order of decreasing aggressiveness. The default value is CONSERVATIVE.

concatenate_vcfs.help_text: Concatenating the germline vcf-files from each applied variant-caller into one vcf-file using bfctools concat.

vep_include_fasta.description: Allow usage of fasta file for annotation with VEP
vep_include_fasta.help_text:
By pointing VEP to a FASTA file, it is possible to retrieve reference sequence locally. This enables VEP to retrieve HGVS notations (--hgvs), check the reference sequence given in input data, and construct transcript models from a GFF or GTF file without accessing a database.

For details, see [here](https://www.ensembl.org/info/docs/tools/vep/script/vep_cache.html#fasta).

vep_dbnsfp.description: Enable the use of the VEP dbNSFP plugin.

dbnsfp.help_text:
To be used with `--vep_dbnsfp`.
dbNSFP files and more information are available at https://www.ensembl.org/info/docs/tools/vep/script/vep_plugins.html#dbnsfp and https://sites.google.com/site/jpopgen/dbNSFP/

dbnsfp_tbi.description: Path to dbNSFP tabix indexed file.

dbnsfp_consequence.help_text:
To be used with `--vep_dbnsfp`.
This params is used to filter/limit outputs to a specific effect of the variant.
The set of consequence terms is defined by the Sequence Ontology and an overview of those used in VEP can be found here: https://www.ensembl.org/info/genome/variation/prediction/predicted_data.html
If one wants to filter using several consequences, then separate those by using '&' (i.e. 'consequence=3_prime_UTR_variant&intron_variant'.

dbnsfp_fields.help_text:
To be used with `--vep_dbnsfp`.
This params can be used to retrieve individual values from the dbNSFP file. The values correspond to the name of the columns in the dbNSFP file and are separated by comma.
The column names might differ between the different dbNSFP versions. Please check the Readme.txt file, which is provided with the dbNSFP file, to obtain the correct column names. The Readme file contains also a short description of the provided values and the version of the tools used to generate them.

Default value are explained below:

rs_dbSNP - rs number from dbSNP
HGVSc_VEP - HGVS coding variant presentation from VEP. Multiple entries separated by ';', corresponds to Ensembl_transcriptid
HGVSp_VEP - HGVS protein variant presentation from VEP. Multiple entries separated by ';', corresponds to Ensembl_proteinid
1000Gp3_EAS_AF - Alternative allele frequency in the 1000Gp3 East Asian descendent samples
1000Gp3_AMR_AF - Alternative allele counts in the 1000Gp3 American descendent samples
LRT_score - Original LRT two-sided p-value (LRTori), ranges from 0 to 1
GERP++_RS - Conservation score. The larger the score, the more conserved the site, ranges from -12.3 to 6.17
gnomAD_exomes_AF - Alternative allele frequency in the whole gnomAD exome samples.

vep_loftee.description: Enable the use of the VEP LOFTEE plugin.

vep_spliceai.description: Enable the use of the VEP SpliceAI plugin.

spliceai_snv.description: Path to spliceai raw scores snv file.

spliceai_snv_tbi.description: Path to spliceai raw scores snv tabix indexed file.

spliceai_indel.description: Path to spliceai raw scores indel file.

spliceai_indel_tbi.description: Path to spliceai raw scores indel tabix indexed file.

vep_spliceregion.description: Enable the use of the VEP SpliceRegion plugin.

vep_custom_args.description: Add an extra custom argument to VEP.
vep_custom_args.help_text: Using this params you can add custom args to VEP.

vep_version.description: Should reflect the VEP version used in the container.
vep_version.help_text: Used by the loftee plugin that need the full path.

outdir_cache.description: The output directory where the cache will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

vep_out_format.help_text: Sets the format of the output-file from VEP. Available formats: json, tab and vcf.

bcftools_annotations.description: A vcf file containing custom annotations to be used with bcftools annotate. Needs to be bgzipped.

bcftools_header_lines.description: Text file with the header lines of `bcftools_annotations`

filter_freebayes.help_text: Apply quality-based filtering specifically to FreeBayes variants. This includes basic quality filters and extraction of high-impact variants.

freebayes_qual_threshold.description: Minimum variant quality score for FreeBayes filtering
freebayes_qual_threshold.help_text: Variants with QUAL score below this threshold will be filtered out.

freebayes_dp_threshold.description: Minimum total depth for FreeBayes variants
freebayes_dp_threshold.help_text: Variants with total depth (DP) below this threshold will be filtered out.

freebayes_af_threshold.description: Minimum allele frequency for FreeBayes variants
freebayes_af_threshold.help_text: Variants with allele frequency (AF) below this threshold will be filtered out.

freebayes_high_impact.help_text: Create separate output files containing only high-impact variants as determined by variant consequence annotations.

general_reference_genome_options.title: General reference genome options
general_reference_genome_options.description: General options to interact with reference genomes.

igenomes_base.description: The base path to the igenomes reference files

igenomes_ignore.description: Do not load the iGenomes reference config.
igenomes_ignore.help_text: Do not load `igenomes.config` when running the pipeline. You may choose this option if you observe clashes between custom parameters and those supplied in `igenomes.config`. **NB** You can then run `Sarek` by specifying at least a FASTA genome file

save_reference.help_text: Set this parameter, if you wish to save all computed reference files. This is useful to avoid re-computation on future runs.

build_only_index.help_text: Set this parameter, if you wish to compute and save all computed reference files. No alignment or any other downstream steps will be performed.

download_cache.help_text:
Set this parameter, if you wish to download annotation cache.
Using this parameter will download cache even if --snpeff_cache and --vep_cache are provided.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

test_data_base.description: Base path / URL for data used in the test profiles
test_data_base.help_text: Warning: The `-profile test` samplesheet file itself contains remote paths. Setting this parameter does not alter the contents of that file.

modules_testdata_base_path.description: Base path / URL for data used in the modules

seq_center.description: Sequencing center information to be added to read group (CN field).

seq_platform.description: Sequencing platform information to be added to read group (PL field).
seq_platform.help_text: Default: ILLUMINA. Will be used to create a proper header for further GATK4 downstream analysis.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

hook_url.description: Incoming hook URL for messaging service
hook_url.help_text: Incoming hook URL for messaging service. Currently, MS Teams and Slack are supported.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files
